title: Blended Scotch
subtitle: 1830 to 1910
description: How a new still, a few grocers and a vine pest made blended Scotch the world's whisky between 1830 and 1910. Four pours.

pours.name: Haig Club Clubman
pours.notes: Grain whisky on its own, which few people taste. Notice how light it is.

pours.name: The Glenlivet 12 Year Old
pours.notes: The malt Usher vatted. Taste it against the grain whisky: heavier, with more fruit and cereal.

pours.name: Johnnie Walker Black Label
pours.notes: Malt and grain together. Look for the fruit of the malt and the lightness of the grain.

pours.name: Dewar’s White Label
pours.notes: Taste a little neat, then try it in a tall glass with ice and soda water, as London drank it in the 1890s.
